Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Church life

council noun

an advisory body

also council of war, council of elders, advisory council, Security Council, church council, synod

classical

Caes. BG 3.3.1
Liv. 30.16.3
M-O s.v. committee, commission

cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n.

noun, second declension

a council, a body of advisers

Counsel, and then the people who give it (Lewis & Short): a general’s council of war, the elders of Carthage, and the Roman senate itself, orbis terrae cōnsilium (Cic. Phil. 4.14). Morgan–Owens gives it for a committee or commission, and Egger for the Security Council, cōnsilium sēcūritātī tuendae.

Examples

  • id erat sānctius apud illōs cōnsilium maximaque ad ipsum senātum regendum vīs

    this was their more sacred council, with the greatest power to guide the senate itself (the thirty elders of Carthage)Liv. 30.16.3

  • cōnsiliō celeriter convocātō sententiās exquīrere coepit

    he quickly called a council and began to ask for opinionsCaes. BG 3.3.1

Other words

  • concilium, conciliī n. — an assembly, a council of delegates

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.30 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. council (eccl.), synod

    An assembly called together to take counsel, as the councils of the Gallic peoples in Caesar; Lewis & Short warn that the manuscripts often confuse it with cōnsilium. The usual word for a council of the Church (Morgan–Owens).

  • synodus, synodī f. — a council of the Church, a synod

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Amm. 15.7.7 (Lewis & Short); Cod. Just. 1.3.23 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. council (eccl.), synod

    Greek σύνοδος: in inscriptions a college of priests, in late Latin an assembly of bishops (Lewis & Short).

See also council, senate, government.

SourcesLewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: concilium · Lewis & Short: synodus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. committee, commission; council (eccl.), synod; United Nations: Security Council.
